title: AI-driven inflation has peaked: Goldman Sachs
key_facts: Goldman economists said AI demand's inflation effect is 'meaningful but moderate' and 'likely near its peak'.
AI price pressures add about 45 basis points to core PCE inflation now.
About half of that reflects a genuine effect rather than mismeasurement.
The effect is expected to peak at 50 basis points by end 2026 and fall to 10 basis points by end 2027.
The fall is expected mainly because memory and computer prices should grow much more slowly.
The Fed raised rates in September, its first rise since July 2023.
New York Fed president John Williams said one more rate hike may be appropriate.
quote_evidence: "In short, the impact of AI demand on inflation is meaningful but moderate, still comes in large part from mismeasurement, and is likely near its peak," Goldman Sachs economists Rindels and David Mericle said in a note on Wednesday.

The economists estimate that AI price pressures are currently boosting "core" Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation by about 45 basis points, of which about half reflects a genuine impact rather than mismeasurement.
why_it_matters_hint: If AI-driven price pressure fades, the Fed may have less reason to keep raising rates.
